subject: Post-call: residency options and fallback constraints for BlueRiver Therapeutics
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluerivertx.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@bluerivertx.com>, Gina Torres <gina.torres@datasec-partners.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency options and fallback constraints for BlueRiver Therapeutics

Thanks for the call earlier Rishi — that recap was helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we share this with legal & infra:  

- We deal with PHI in some integrations; any log-level data that might contain PII/PHI needs to be either redacted or sent only to our secure S3 (US-EAST-1) with customer-managed keys. Is that supported today?  
- Our procurement team wants a clear statement on cross-region failover: if US-EAST capacity is unavailable, will requests be routed to US-WEST or to a European region? We need the default behavior and whether we can pin strictly to a single region.  
- Retention: for audit we're looking at a 90-day rolling retention for request/response bodies, plus 7 years for aggregated logs. Can Redwood provide configurable retention windows at the workspace level?

If you can put these points in a single doc that we can pass to security, that'd be great. Sam, tagging you to make sure I captured product requirements correctly.

— Alex
Lead Integrations Engineer
BlueRiver Therapeutics

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluerivertx.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@bluerivertx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Gina Torres <gina.torres@datasec-partners.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency options and fallback constraints for BlueRiver Therapeutics

Alex — thanks, appreciate the precise asks. I put together the short answers below and attached a one-pager (redwood-residency-factsheet.pdf) and a working draft MAP (blueRiver-draft-map.docx) you can circulate with legal/legaltechnical. High level answers:  

1) PII/PHI and logging: Redwood supports both payload redaction and workspace-level routing of logs. You can:  
   - Enable in-flight and at-rest encryption with a customer-managed KMS key (we support AWS KMS and key import flows).  
   - Route raw request/response payloads to a customer-owned S3 bucket (US-EAST-1) — we never persist that data in our hosted logs when that route is enabled.  
   - For platform-level telemetry and aggregated metrics we offer a separate export that strips payload fields; full audit logs (who/when) are available and can be configured to avoid storing message text.  

2) Cross-region failover & pinning: 
   - Default hosted behavior: smart-routing prefers pinned region; if pinned capacity is exhausted and policy allows, traffic can fail over to a compatible region for availability.  
   - We offer strict pinning: you can opt into "hard pin" which prevents cross-region fallback (useful for strict residency requirements). That will surface errors if capacity is unavailable.  
   - For BlueRiver we recommend a warm-standby in US-WEST with cold fallback to EU only if you accept cross-border transit in your contract (we flagged this as a legal decision).

3) Retention controls: 
   - Workspace-level retention policy configurable in console (options: 0, 30, 90, 365, custom up to 7 years).
   - Audit logs stored separately with configurable retention; exported artifacts can be sent to your S3/GCS for long-term archival.

Next steps I've suggested in the attached MAP: agree on (A) pin policy (hard vs soft), (B) KMS vs Redwood-managed keys, (C) retention windows for each data class (payloads, audit logs, metrics). Would you be able to confirm preferred choices so we can scope procurement and a dedicated quoting exercise?

I'll loop in Marissa & Vivek for detailed SLA/ops and security answers — tagging them below.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-residency-factsheet.pdf (summary of pinning & routing options)
- blueRiver-draft-map.docx (working MAP - fillable)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluerivertx.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Gina Torres <gina.torres@datasec-partners.com>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency options and fallback constraints for BlueRiver Therapeutics

Alex — quick operational clarifications from my side (solutions/ops):

- Backup cadence and encryption: snapshots of model state and indexes taken daily; backups can be pushed to your S3 with SSE-KMS using your CMK. If you choose hard pin, backups remain in the pinned region by default.
- Failover behavior specifics: if you select soft pin + routing policy with "region_preference=us-east", we will try UEAST -> US-WEST (warm standbys) before considering cross-border options; explicit cross-border fallback requires signed authorization.
- Throttling and capacity: hard pinning can increase error rates under load — we typically recommend reserved capacity for predictable throughput. We can produce an ops playbook for cutover/failback drills.

Action items:
1) Alex/Sam: indicate hard vs soft pin preference and whether BlueRiver will accept backups to your S3 in US-EAST (yes/no).
2) Rishi: can you share a rough monthly QPS and 95th pct token estimate so I can size reserved capacity?
3) Vivek: please confirm if you want a security call to walk through KMS import and key rotation cadence.

— Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluerivertx.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Gina Torres <gina.torres@datasec-partners.com>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency options and fallback constraints for BlueRiver Therapeutics

Alex / Sam — happy to run a focused security session. Two notes before that call:  

1) KMS & key import: if you import a customer key we can configure our control plane to use your CMK for encrypting at-rest artifacts sent to your S3. We will not have access to the key material. Key rotation is supported; we recommend a 90-day rotation window for keys that protect PHI.
2) Redaction vs routing: redaction is best-effort and relies on deterministic PII patterns; for PHI we recommend routing raw payloads directly to your bucket (no copy kept in Redwood logs). We log metadata ( who/when/request id ) for auditing but can exclude request bodies if routing is enabled.

I'll schedule a 45-minute technical follow-up. Please propose two time slots next week and include any security/infosec folks from your side.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
